title: Hepatitis A test
what: This blood test looks for antibodies to the hepatitis A virus. It shows whether you have it now or are already protected.
why: For yellow skin, dark urine, weakness, and nausea, after contact with someone who has it, or before a hepatitis A vaccine.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you were in contact with someone who has hepatitis A
If you had a hepatitis A vaccine
If your skin or eyes are turning yellow

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast strictly, but it is better to come 3 to 4 hours after a light, non-fatty meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours: no alcohol and no hard workouts. Try not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop anything on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything needs to change before the test.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A sleeve you can easily roll up above the elbow.

bring: Your referral or list of tests
Your vaccination records, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied above your elbow, and you are asked to clench your fist a few times
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick. Blood fills the tubes in a few seconds
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
If you have symptoms, wash your hands after using the toilet, and do not cook for others until you get the result
Your doctor will explain the result
red_flags: Yellow skin, severe weakness, or vomiting: see a doctor the same day
Confusion, extreme sleepiness, or bleeding: call emergency services

faq.q: What do the different antibodies mean?
faq.a: IgM antibodies usually mean the illness is happening now. IgG antibodies mean you had it before or were vaccinated.
Through dirty hands, water, and food. Hand washing and the vaccine protect well.

reminders.text: Hepatitis A test tomorrow. Better to skip fatty food in the morning.
